campaignId.description: ID of the email campaign to retrieve. Example: 1

statistics.description: Optional filter to return only the selected statistics section of the campaign. Omit to return all statistics.

excludeHtmlContent.description: When true, the htmlContent field is returned as an empty string. Defaults to false.

previewText.description: Preview text (preheader) of the campaign email

createdAt.description: Date-time of creation of the campaign, as an ISO 8601 timestamp with a provider-determined UTC offset (e.g. "2026-10-01T20:22:21.000+03:00"), not necessarily "Z"/UTC.

modifiedAt.description: Date-time of the last modification of the campaign, as an ISO 8601 timestamp with a provider-determined UTC offset (e.g. "2026-10-01T20:22:32.000+03:00"), not necessarily "Z"/UTC.

actions.description: Retrieve a single transactional email template's detail.

templateId.description: ID of the template to retrieve. Accepts the numeric template ID (e.g. 6) or a custom template identifier string assigned at creation.

id.description: Unique numeric ID of the template

subject.description: Subject line of the template email

isActive.description: Whether the template is active

name.description: Name of the sender for the template

createdAt.description: Creation UTC date-time of the template (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ)

modifiedAt.description: Last modification UTC date-time of the template (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ)

modifiedAt.description: Date-time at which the campaign was last modified, as an ISO 8601 timestamp with a provider-determined UTC offset (e.g. "2023-01-20T14:53:02.000+01:00"), not necessarily "Z"/UTC.

lists.description: Recipient contact lists, returned as objects with id and name

actions.description: Retrieve the transactional email event log (requests, delivered, opens, clicks, bounces, etc.) for the account.
actions.name: get-transactional-email-events

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return. Example: 100. Defaults to 2500 on the provider side when omitted.

offset.description: Beginning point in the result list to retrieve from (0-based). Defaults to 0.

email.description: Filter the report for a specific recipient email address. Example: "john.smith@example.com".

event.description: Filter the report for a specific event type. Example: "delivered".

templateId.description: Filter on a specific transactional template ID. Example: 4.

messageId.description: Filter on a specific message ID. Example: "<201798300811.5787683@example.domain.com>".

startDate.description: Starting date of the report (YYYY-MM-DD). Mandatory if endDate is used and must be lower than or equal to endDate. When no dates are passed, the report covers the past 30 days.

endDate.description: Ending date of the report (YYYY-MM-DD). Mandatory if startDate is used and must be greater than or equal to startDate. The date range cannot exceed 90 days.

ActionInput_brevo_api_key_gettransaction.description: Filters for the transactional email event log. All fields are optional; with no startDate/endDate the provider returns the past 30 days.

date.description: Date-time on which the event was generated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp with a provider-determined UTC offset (e.g. "2026-09-30T12:30:00+03:00"), not necessarily "Z"/UTC.

email.description: Email address which generated the event.

event.description: Event which occurred (e.g. requests, delivered, opened, clicks, hardBounces).

messageId.description: Message ID which generated the event.

from.description: Sender email address from which the email was sent.

ip.description: IP from which the recipient opened the email or clicked a link (only present on opened/clicks events).

link.description: Link that was sent to the recipient (only present on requests/opened/clicks events).

reason.description: Reason of the bounce (only present on hardBounces/softBounces events).

subject.description: Subject of the email.

tag.description: Tag of the email which generated the event.

templateId.description: ID of the transactional template used (only present when the email is template based).

events.description: Transactional email events matching the filters, newest first by default. Empty when nothing matches the filters.

ActionOutput_brevo_api_key_gettransactio.description: The transactional email event log for the account.

actions.description: Link or unlink contacts and/or companies to a deal.

actions.description: List the account's contact attribute schema (built-in and custom fields such as FIRSTNAME/LASTNAME).

name.description: Attribute name as used in contact attribute payloads. Example: "FIRSTNAME"

actions.description: List the account's contact folders (the organizational containers for lists)

actions.description: List granular activity events (opens, clicks, replies, bounces, sends, etc.) for a campaign and/or a specific lead.
actions.name: list-campaign-activities

campaignId.description: Filter activities to a single campaign. Omit to include activities from every campaign in the team. Example: "cam_123"

leadId.description: Filter activities to a single lead. This is the campaign-scoped lead ID (lea_...) as returned when the lead was added to a campaign, not the account-wide contactId. Example: "lea_123"

type.description: Filter by activity type. Exact spelling matters: email types are plural (emailsOpened), LinkedIn invite types are linkedinInvite*. The provider rejects unknown values with a 400.

limit.description: Number of activities to return per request, between 1 and 100. Defaults to 100.

offset.description: Number of activities to skip. To page through results, increment this by the limit on each request. Defaults to 0.

minDate.description: Return only activities with createdAt at or after this value. Accepts an ISO 8601 datetime (e.g. "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z") or a Unix timestamp in seconds (e.g. "1715385600").

maxDate.description: Return only activities with createdAt at or before this value. Accepts an ISO 8601 datetime or a Unix timestamp in seconds. Must be strictly greater than minDate when both are set.

ActionInput_lemlist_listcampaignactiviti.description: Filters for the lemlist activities feed. All fields are optional; with no filters the feed returns activities across all campaigns.

type.description: Activity type, e.g. "emailsSent", "emailsOpened", "emailsClicked", "emailsReplied" or "emailsBounced". Matches the lemlist ActivityType enum used by the type filter.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the activity occurred. Example: "2025-10-28T08:07:38.375Z"

campaignId.description: ID of the campaign the activity belongs to. Absent on activities that are not tied to a campaign. Example: "cam_bSn8EORHQxbWPjHvu"

campaignName.description: Name of the campaign the activity belongs to, when the activity is tied to a campaign.

leadId.description: Campaign-scoped ID of the lead the activity relates to. Absent when the activity is not tied to a lead. Example: "lea_fiDpiGV585wy3Oii2"

contactId.description: Account-wide contact ID the activity relates to. Example: "ctc_xW8Ou6C03Csv8vatp"

leadEmail.description: Lead email address as it was when the activity happened. Present on campaign activities only.

leadFirstName.description: Lead first name as it was when the activity happened. Campaign activities only, and only if the lead had this variable set at that moment.

leadLastName.description: Lead last name as it was when the activity happened. Same scope as leadFirstName.

leadCompanyName.description: Lead company name as it was when the activity happened. Same scope as leadFirstName.

sequenceId.description: ID of the sequence that produced the activity. Example: "seq_ODjsLXkxXiySRw6dK"

stepId.description: Stable identifier of the sequence step that produced the activity. Absent on older activities recorded before step-level tracking existed.

sequenceStep.description: Zero-based position of the step within the sequence at the time of the activity. Shifts when sequence steps are reordered; prefer stepId for a stable reference.

totalSequenceStep.description: Zero-based count of the sequence steps already delivered to this lead when the activity occurred.

activities.description: Activity events matching the requested filters.

nextOffset.description: Offset to pass as offset to fetch the next page. Present only when this page is full (its size equals the requested limit), meaning more activities may exist. A follow-up request can still return an empty page when the total is an exact multiple of the limit.

ActionOutput_lemlist_listcampaignactivit.description: The matching activity events plus the offset to fetch the next page when more results may exist.

message.description: Human-readable provider error message when the job could not be started. Present only when started is false.

ActionOutput_lemlist_verifyemail.description: Outcome of requesting an asynchronous email-address verification. The verification result itself is retrieved separately with the returned job ID.

syncs.description: Sync every lead enrolled in every campaign
syncs.name: campaign-leads

id.description: Stable record id scoped to the parent campaign, formatted as `${campaignId}:${leadId}`. The lemlist lead id is only unique within its campaign, so the campaign id is prepended to avoid collisions across campaigns.

campaignId.description: Identifier of the campaign this lead enrollment belongs to. Example: cam_vyzp8v33RBTfNQRvz

leadId.description: Campaign-scoped lemlist lead identifier (the `_id` field of the campaign leads list). Example: lea_K38DYz3t7pyzATMZF

contactId.description: Account-wide contact identifier. Unlike leadId, this is stable across campaigns for the same person and can be used to join with other lemlist contacts. Example: ctc_jgZq5fmsGxkmSd7x4

state.description: Last reported state of the lead within this campaign, e.g. scanned, contacted, interested. Note: lemlist does not update this value when a lead is later removed or unsubscribed, so it reflects the state at the last reported activity rather than live membership.

CampaignLead.description: A lead enrolled in a lemlist campaign, as listed by the campaign leads endpoint.

syncs.description: Full refresh of every lemlist campaign in the team (name, status, sequence id, creator). Note: lemlist has no campaign-deletion API, so a record flagged as deleted only means the campaign no longer appears in GET /api/campaigns (e.g. excluded by a filter the endpoint does not expose), not that it was actually destroyed.
syncs.name: campaigns

id.description: The campaign's unique lemlist identifier (the `_id` field). Example: 'cam_vyzp8v33RBTfNQRvz'

status.description: The campaign's lifecycle status as reported by the list endpoint, e.g. 'draft', 'running' or 'paused'

sequenceId.description: Identifier of the campaign's messaging sequence. Example: 'seq_8Xp3uSRQrBAdTGffc'

emoji.description: The campaign's emoji icon, when one is set

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the campaign was created

createdBy.description: Lemlist user id of the campaign's creator. Example: 'usr_22HzEMYb8ZvdNstrC'

Campaign.description: A lemlist campaign with its core metadata as returned by GET /api/campaigns

labelId.description: The identifier of the label to add. Example: "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174001"

actions.name: archive-cycle

id.description: The identifier of the cycle to archive. Example: "cycle-uuid"

id.description: The identifier of the issue to archive. Example: "c0b0b0b0-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" or "TEAM-123"

actions.description: Create an attachment on a Linear issue.

issueId.description: The issue to associate the attachment with. Can be a UUID or issue identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Example: "590a1127-f98b-49fc-ba74-2df8751c089e"

url.description: Attachment location which is also used as a unique identifier for the attachment. Example: "https://example.com/123"

iconUrl.description: An icon url to display with the attachment. Should be of jpg or png format. Example: "https://example.com/icon.png"

metadata.description: Attachment metadata object with string and number values. Example: {"exceptionId": "exc-123"}

groupBySource.description: Indicates if attachments for the same source application should be grouped in the Linear UI.

createAsUser.description: Create attachment as a user with the provided name. This option is only available to OAuth applications creating attachments in actor=application mode.

commentBody.description: Create a linked comment with markdown body.

body.description: The comment body content.

parentId.description: The ID of the parent comment for threaded replies.

name.description: The name of the cycle. Example: "Sprint 23"

startsAt.description: The start date of the cycle in ISO 8601 format. Example: "2024-01-15T00:00:00Z"

endsAt.description: The end date of the cycle in ISO 8601 format. Example: "2024-01-29T00:00:00Z"

completedAt.description: The completion date of the cycle in ISO 8601 format.

color.description: The color of the label as a HEX string. Example: "#EB5757"

teamId.description: The identifier of the team to associate the label with. If omitted, the label will be workspace-level.

type.description: Type of relationship between the issues.

actions.description: Create a relationship link between two records via a navigation property.
actions.name: associate-records

entitySetName.description: Entity set (collection) name of the primary record that owns the relationship, e.g. "contacts". Use the list-entity-definitions action to discover the entity set names available in the org.

id.description: GUID of the primary record that owns the navigation property. Example: "ed1c5323-2bbc-f111-aaad-7ced8d717fa5"

navigationProperty.description: Schema name of the navigation property on the primary record, e.g. "parentcustomerid_account" to link a contact to its parent account.

relationshipType.description: Whether navigationProperty is a single-valued navigation property (a lookup field such as "parentcustomerid_account", which Dataverse associates with PUT) or a collection-valued navigation property (a one-to-many "many" side or many-to-many relationship, which Dataverse associates with POST). This cannot be inferred from the property name alone; look it up via list-entity-attributes/list-entity-definitions or the relationship metadata for the entity if unsure.

relatedEntitySetName.description: Entity set (collection) name of the related record to link to, e.g. "accounts".

relatedId.description: GUID of the related record to link. Example: "e91c5323-2bbc-f111-aaad-7ced8d717fa5"

environmentUrl.description: Host name of the Dataverse environment (org URL) from the connection configuration, with or without the https:// prefix, e.g. "org98374485.crm.dynamics.com". Dataverse requires the related record to be referenced by its absolute URL.

ActionInput_microsoft_dataverse_associat.description: Parameters for linking two records: the primary record, the navigation property on it, the related record to link, and the org URL used to build the absolute related-record URL that Dataverse requires.

success.description: True when Dataverse accepted the association (HTTP 204 No Content).

ActionOutput_microsoft_dataverse_associa.description: Result of the association request. Dataverse returns 204 No Content on success, so this only confirms the link was accepted.

actions.description: Update an opportunity's fields.
actions.name: update-opportunity

opportunityId.description: GUID of the opportunity to update. Example: "e90a0493-e8f0-ea11-a815-000d3a1b14a2"

name.description: Topic of the opportunity. Maps to the name attribute, which Dataverse requires, so it cannot be cleared with null.

description.description: Detailed description of the opportunity. Pass null to clear the current value.

estimatedValue.description: Estimated revenue in the opportunity's transaction currency. Maps to estimatedvalue. Pass null to clear.

estimatedCloseDate.description: Estimated close date as "YYYY-MM-DD" or an ISO 8601 datetime. Maps to estimatedclosedate. Pass null to clear.

closeProbability.description: Close probability between 0 and 100. Maps to closeprobability. Pass null to clear.

budgetAmount.description: Customer's budget in the opportunity's transaction currency. Maps to budgetamount. Pass null to clear.

currentSituation.description: Notes on the customer's current situation. Maps to currentsituation. Pass null to clear.

customerNeed.description: Notes on the customer's need. Maps to customerneed. Pass null to clear.

proposedSolution.description: Notes on the proposed solution. Maps to proposedsolution. Pass null to clear.

salesStageCode.description: Sales stage option-set value; 1 is the only option in a default org. Maps to salesstagecode. Pass null to clear.

purchaseProcess.description: Customer's purchase process: 0 = Individual, 1 = Committee, 2 = Unknown. Maps to purchaseprocess. Pass null to clear.

purchaseTimeframe.description: Purchase timeframe: 0 = Immediate, 1 = This Quarter, 2 = Next Quarter, 3 = This Year, 4 = Unknown. Maps to purchasetimeframe. Pass null to clear.

need.description: Customer's level of need: 0 = Must have, 1 = Should have, 2 = Good to have, 3 = No need. Maps to need. Pass null to clear.

discountAmount.description: Discount amount in the opportunity's transaction currency. Maps to discountamount. Pass null to clear.

discountPercentage.description: Discount percentage applied to the opportunity. Maps to discountpercentage. Pass null to clear.

freightAmount.description: Freight amount in the opportunity's transaction currency. Maps to freightamount. Pass null to clear.

statusCode.description: Status reason for an opportunity that is still open: 1 = In Progress or 2 = On Hold. Maps to statuscode. This action performs a plain PATCH with no statecode change, so it cannot close an opportunity: closed-state reasons (3 = Won, 4 = Canceled, 5 = Out-Sold) are rejected. Use Dataverse's dedicated WinOpportunity/LoseOpportunity bound actions to win or lose an opportunity, which this action does not implement. This field is required by Dataverse once set and cannot be cleared with null.

description.description: Detailed notes for the phone call.

phonenumber.description: Phone number dialed, in free-text form. Example: "930-555-0168"

statecode.description: State of the phone call: 0 = Open, 1 = Completed, 2 = Canceled, 3 = Scheduled.

statuscode.description: Detailed status reason of the phone call (e.g. 1 = Open, 2 = Made, 3 = Received, 4 = Canceled).

prioritycode.description: Priority of the phone call: 0 = Low, 1 = Normal, 2 = High.

scheduledstart.description: Scheduled start time of the call (ISO 8601 UTC). Example: "2026-09-16T03:30:00Z"

scheduledend.description: Scheduled end time of the call (ISO 8601 UTC).

actualstart.description: Actual start time of the call (ISO 8601 UTC).

actualend.description: Actual end time of the call (ISO 8601 UTC).

actualdurationminutes.description: Actual duration of the call in minutes. Example: 6

regardingobjectid.description: GUID of the parent record this call is regarding (e.g. an account, contact, lead, or opportunity).

ownerid.description: GUID of the user or team that owns the phone call.

createdby.description: GUID of the user who created the phone call record.

modifiedby.description: GUID of the user who last modified the phone call record.

createdon.description: Timestamp when the record was created (ISO 8601 UTC). Example: "2026-09-18T19:43:40Z"

modifiedon.description: Timestamp when the record was last modified (ISO 8601 UTC). The incremental sync cursor is the Dataverse versionnumber, not this field.

syncs.description: Sync task activities from Microsoft Dataverse, incrementally on `versionnumber`, with a periodic full refresh to detect deletions.

id.description: Unique identifier of the task record (the Dataverse `activityid` GUID). Example: "f6f57339-4687-eb11-a812-000d3a09c1c0"

subject.description: Subject or short title of the task.

description.description: Full description or body text of the task.

scheduledstart.description: Scheduled start time of the task as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

scheduledend.description: Scheduled end (due) time of the task as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

actualdurationminutes.description: Actual duration of the task in minutes.

prioritycode.description: Priority of the task as a Dataverse option-set value (0 = Low, 1 = Normal, 2 = High).

statecode.description: State of the task as a Dataverse option-set value (0 = Open, 1 = Completed, 2 = Canceled).

statuscode.description: Detailed status of the task as a Dataverse option-set value, tied to `statecode`.

regardingobjectid.description: GUID of the parent record this task is regarding, e.g. an account or contact (from the `_regardingobjectid_value` lookup).

modifiedon.description: Timestamp the task was last modified, as an ISO 8601 UTC string. The incremental sync cursor is the Dataverse versionnumber, not this field.

name.description: Display name of the team. Example: "org98374485".

teamtype.description: Team type option-set value: 0 = Owner, 1 = Access, 2 = Microsoft Entra security group, 3 = Microsoft Entra Office group.

businessunitid.description: GUID of the business unit the team belongs to.

administratorid.description: GUID of the systemuser who administers the team.

modifiedon.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the team was last modified. The incremental sync cursor is the Dataverse versionnumber, not this field. Example: "2026-09-17T13:28:57Z".

syncs.description: Incrementally sync Microsoft Dataverse system users (systemusers), with a weekly full refresh to detect hard-deleted users.

firstname.description: First name of the user. Omitted when null upstream.

lastname.description: Last name of the user. Omitted when null upstream.

internalemailaddress.description: Primary internal email address of the user, e.g. "ada@fabrikam.com". Omitted when null upstream.

actions.description: Update the given field(s) on up to 1000 issues at once, selected by id or by the current search query.
actions.name: bulk-update-issues

organization_id_or_slug.description: The ID or slug of the organization the issues belong to. Example: "my-org".

ids.description: Numeric issue IDs to update, as decimal strings (matching the id field returned by the list-issues actions), sent as repeated id query parameters. Required for non-status updates; optional for status updates, where omitting it updates all issues matching the filters. Maximum 1000. Example: ["123456789"].

query.description: Search query selecting issues when ids is omitted (status updates only). The provider defaults to "is:unresolved" when unset; pass an empty string to match all issues. Example: "is:unresolved browser:Chrome".

project.description: Project IDs or slugs restricting the selection. Omit to include all accessible projects; "-1" also selects all accessible projects. Example: ["web-frontend", "123456789"].

environment.description: Environment names to filter the selection by. Example: ["production"].

statsPeriod.description: Time window for the selection query, a number followed by d, h, m, s, or w. Overrides start and end. Example: "24h".

start.description: ISO-8601 start of the selection time window. Example: "2026-01-01T00:00:00".

end.description: ISO-8601 end of the selection time window. Example: "2026-01-02T00:00:00".

limit.description: Maximum number of issues affected when selecting via filters. Provider maximum is 100.

inbox.description: If true, marks the issues as reviewed by the requestor.

status.description: New status for the selected issues.

inNextRelease.description: If true, marks the issues as resolved in the next release.

inRelease.description: Release version the issues are resolved in. The value "latest" resolves them in the most recent release.

inCommit.description: Commit the issues should be marked as resolved in.

commit.description: SHA of the resolving commit. Example: "2bcba4a1e2932e7b3a0fdd2a68d20c34e8f1a2b3".

repository.description: Name of the repository as it appears in Sentry. Example: "my-org/my-repo".

ignoreDuration.description: Ignore the issues for this many minutes.

ignoreCount.description: Ignore the issues until each has occurred this many times within ignoreWindow minutes.

ignoreWindow.description: Window in minutes over which ignoreCount is measured. Maximum 10080 (1 week).

ignoreUserCount.description: Ignore the issues until each has affected this many users within ignoreUserWindow minutes.

ignoreUserWindow.description: Window in minutes over which ignoreUserCount is measured. Maximum 10080 (1 week).

statusDetails.description: Additional details about the resolution. Status detail updates that include release data are only allowed for issues within a single project.

substatus.description: New substatus for the selected issues; null clears it.

hasSeen.description: If true, marks the issues as seen by the requestor.

isBookmarked.description: If true, bookmarks the issues for the requestor; false removes the bookmark.

isPublic.description: If true, publishes the issues with a public share link; false unpublishes them.

isSubscribed.description: If true, subscribes the requestor to the issues.

merge.description: If true, merges the selected issues together. This cannot be undone.

discard.description: If true, discards the selected issues instead of updating them. Discarded issues are deleted and matching future events are dropped.

assignedTo.description: User or team to assign the issues to, as "<user_id>", "user:<user_id>", "<username>", "<user_primary_email>", or "team:<team_id>". Pass an empty string to unassign.

priority.description: Priority to set on the selected issues.

actions.description: Get event counts for the organization grouped and time-bucketed by an arbitrary dimension (category, project, outcome, etc.).

organization_id_or_slug.description: The ID or slug of the organization to query event counts for. Example: "nangodev".

groupBy.description: Dimension(s) to group counts by. Pass multiple values to group by multiple dimensions, e.g. ["project", "outcome"].

field.description: Aggregation to compute per group and interval. "sum(quantity)" is the event count (bytes for attachments); "sum(times_seen)" counts how many times an event has been seen.

statsPeriod.description: Relative time window in <number><unit> format, e.g. "24h" or "7d" (units: m, h, d, w). Provide either this or both start and end; defaults to the last 90 days.

interval.description: Resolution of the time series in the same <number><unit> format as statsPeriod. At most "1d", and must evenly divide one day (1440 minutes), e.g. "1h", "6h", "12h", "1d".

start.description: Start of the time window as a UTC ISO 8601 datetime or epoch seconds. Use together with end instead of statsPeriod. Example: "2026-09-28T00:00:00Z".

end.description: Inclusive end of the time window as a UTC ISO 8601 datetime or epoch seconds. Use together with start instead of statsPeriod.

project.description: Project IDs to filter by. Use ["-1"] to include all accessible projects. Example: ["4512170111991808"].

category.description: Filter by data category, e.g. "error" for error events or "transaction" for transaction events. "attachment", "profile_duration", "profile_duration_ui" and "profile_chunk_ui" cannot be combined with other categories.

outcome.description: Filter by outcome status, e.g. "accepted" for stored events or "rate_limited" for events dropped by rate limiting.

reason.description: Filter by the reason events were filtered or dropped, e.g. "spike_protection".

ActionInput_sentry_getorganizationeventc.description: Dimensions, aggregation field, time window, and filters for the organization event-counts query.

start.description: Start of the resolved time window as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

end.description: End of the resolved time window as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

intervals.description: Start timestamp of each time bucket as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. Omitted when grouping by project.

by.description: Values of the requested groupBy dimensions for this group, e.g. {"category": "error"} or {"project": 4512170111991808, "outcome": "accepted"}.

totals.description: Total for each requested field (keyed by field name, e.g. "sum(quantity)") across the entire time window.

series.description: Per-interval value for each requested field, aligned with the top-level intervals array. Omitted when grouping by project, which returns totals only.

items.description: Event counts for one distinct combination of groupBy dimension values.

groups.description: One entry per distinct combination of groupBy dimension values found in the time window.

projectID.description: Numeric ID of the Sentry project that ingested the event, e.g. "4512170111991808"

groupID.description: Numeric ID of the issue (group) this event belongs to; omitted when the event is not grouped into an issue

title.description: Human-readable event title, e.g. "TypeError: undefined is not a function"

message.description: Event message as sent by the SDK

location.description: File or function location where the event occurred

culprit.description: Function or module Sentry identified as the cause of the event

platform.description: SDK platform that sent the event, e.g. "node"

dateCreated.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when Sentry ingested the event, e.g. "2026-09-29T15:04:05.000Z"; omitted on the rare event Sentry cannot date

eventType.description: Sentry event type, e.g. "error" or "default" (maps the provider field "event.type")

user.description: User context attached to the event, when Sentry could associate one

id.description: ID of the user associated with the event, when known

email.description: Email address of the user associated with the event, when known

username.description: Username of the user associated with the event, when known

ip_address.description: IP address of the user associated with the event, when known

name.description: Display name of the user associated with the event, when known

geo.description: Approximate geolocation (country, region, city) derived from the user IP address

data.description: Additional free-form user attributes sent with the event

tags.description: Tags attached to the event

items.description: Key/value tag attached to the event

crashFile.description: Reference to an attached crash file (e.g. minidump), when present

metadata.description: Free-form event metadata as returned by Sentry (e.g. title, filename, function)

Event.description: A Sentry event ingested by a project (summary payload; the full event body with stacktrace is not included)

syncs.description: Sync issues (error groups) across all projects in the organization.
syncs.name: issues

id.description: Numeric issue ID as a string; used in Sentry API path parameters. Example: "7761433611"

shortId.description: Human-readable issue short ID shown in the Sentry UI and permalinks. Example: "NANGO-SEED-PROJECT-1"

title.description: Issue title, usually the error type and value. Example: "TypeError: undefined is not a function"

culprit.description: Legacy culprit string describing where the error occurred.

permalink.description: URL of the issue details page in Sentry.

level.description: Severity level of the issue. Example: "error"

status.description: Resolution status of the issue: "unresolved", "resolved" or "ignored".

substatus.description: Sub-status of the issue, e.g. "archived_until_escalating" for ignored issues.

logger.description: Logger that reported the issue's events, when set.

platform.description: Platform of the events grouped into this issue. Example: "node"

type.description: Grouping type of the issue, e.g. "error" or "default".

priority.description: Issue priority: "high", "medium" or "low".

count.description: Number of events grouped into this issue, serialized as a string. Example: "150"

userCount.description: Number of distinct users affected by this issue.

numComments.description: Number of comments on the issue.

isPublic.description: Whether the issue has been shared publicly.

isBookmarked.description: Whether the token's user has bookmarked the issue.

isSubscribed.description: Whether the token's user is subscribed to the issue.

hasSeen.description: Whether the token's user has seen the issue.

isUnhandled.description: Whether the issue's events were unhandled exceptions.

annotations.description: Annotation strings attached to the issue, e.g. rendered links to external issues.

project.description: The Sentry project the issue belongs to.

id.description: Numeric ID (as a string) of the project the issue belongs to. Example: "4512170111991808"

slug.description: Slug of the project, unique within the organization. Example: "nango-seed-project"

platform.description: Platform key of the project. Example: "node"

metadata.description: Issue metadata extracted from the ingested event payload.

title.description: Human-readable title generated by Sentry for the issue.

type.description: Error type for error issues, usually the exception class. Example: "TypeError"

value.description: Error value or message for error issues. Example: "undefined is not a function"

filename.description: File in which the error occurred, when known.

function.description: Function in which the error occurred, when known.

assignedTo.description: User or team the issue is currently assigned to. Omitted when unassigned.

type.description: Type of the assignee actor, either "user" or "team". Example: "user"

id.description: ID of the assigned user or team, as a string. Example: "15174593"

name.description: Display name of the assigned user or team. Example: "John Doe"

email.description: Email of the assigned user. Present for user assignees only. Example: "john.doe@example.com"

firstRelease.description: The first release in which the issue was seen, when the issue is bound to a release.

version.description: Version string of the release. Example: "nango-seed-1.0.0"

firstSeen.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the first event grouped into this issue. Example: "2018-11-06T21:19:55Z"

lastSeen.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the most recent event grouped into this issue. Example: "2018-12-06T21:19:55Z"

Issue.description: A Sentry issue (error group) from any project in the organization.

syncs.description: Sync organization members.

email.description: Email address the membership is bound to, e.g. api@nango.dev.

name.description: Display name of the member. Defaults to the email address.

orgRole.description: Organization-level role of the member, e.g. owner, manager, member or billing.

pending.description: Whether the membership invite is still pending acceptance.

expired.description: Whether the membership invite has expired.

inviteStatus.description: Invite approval status, e.g. approved, requested_to_be_invited or requested_to_join.

inviterName.description: Name of the member who sent the invite, or null when the member was not invited by anyone.

dateCreated.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the membership was created, e.g. 2026-09-29T14:09:02.084485Z.

id.description: Unique ID of the linked Sentry user account, e.g. 5026258.

name.description: Display name of the user. Defaults to the email address.

username.description: Username of the user. Defaults to the email address.

email.description: Email address of the user, e.g. api@nango.dev.

avatarUrl.description: URL of the user avatar image.

isActive.description: Whether the user account is active.

has2fa.description: Whether the user has two-factor authentication enabled.

isManaged.description: Whether the user account is managed by an external identity provider.

isStaff.description: Whether the user is a Sentry staff account.

isSuperuser.description: Whether the user is a Sentry superuser.

isSuspended.description: Whether the user account is suspended.

hasPasswordAuth.description: Whether the user can authenticate with a password.

dateJoined.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the user account was created, e.g. 2026-09-29T14:09:00.725342Z.

lastLogin.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last login, or null if the user has never logged in.

lastActive.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last user activity, or null if the user has never been active.

anyOf.description: Sentry user account linked to the membership.

user.description: Sentry user account linked to the membership, or null while the invite is pending and no user account is linked yet.

Member.description: A Sentry organization member with its organization role and, once the invite is accepted, the linked user account.

syncs.description: Sync cron monitors for a Sentry organization, including schedule configuration and nested monitor environments.
syncs.name: monitors

id.description: Unique Sentry ID of the cron monitor (UUID).

slug.description: URL-safe slug of the monitor, unique within the organization.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the monitor (e.g. 'active', 'disabled', 'pending_deletion').

isMuted.description: Whether the monitor is muted and does not create issues.

isUpserting.description: Whether the monitor was created implicitly by a check-in upsert.

dateCreated.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the monitor was created.

schedule_type.description: Schedule syntax used by the monitor: 'crontab' for a crontab expression or 'interval' for a fixed interval.

schedule.description: Crontab expression (e.g. '0 * * * *') when schedule_type is 'crontab', or a [count, unit] tuple (e.g. [1, 'day']) when schedule_type is 'interval'.

checkin_margin.description: Minutes after the expected check-in time before the check-in is considered missed. Null when the monitor uses the Sentry default.

max_runtime.description: Minutes a check-in may stay in progress before it is considered failed. Null when the monitor uses the Sentry default.

timezone.description: IANA time zone the crontab schedule is evaluated in (e.g. 'America/Los_Angeles'). Null when unset.

failure_issue_threshold.description: Number of consecutive failed check-ins before an issue is created. Null when disabled.

recovery_threshold.description: Number of consecutive successful check-ins before a monitor issue is resolved. Null when disabled.

alert_rule_id.description: Legacy ID of the alert rule attached to this monitor. Null when no alert rule is attached.

config.description: Schedule and check-in tolerance configuration of the monitor.

id.description: Numeric Sentry ID of the project the monitor belongs to.

slug.description: URL-safe slug of the project the monitor belongs to.

name.description: Display name of the project the monitor belongs to.

platform.description: SDK platform key of the project (e.g. 'node'). Null when the project has no platform set.

project.description: Project the monitor belongs to.

status.description: Health status of the monitor in this environment (e.g. 'ok', 'error', 'missed_checkin').

isMuted.description: Whether the monitor environment is muted and does not create issues.

dateCreated.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the monitor environment was created.

lastCheckIn.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent check-in in this environment. Null when no check-in was ever received.

nextCheckIn.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the next check-in is expected in this environment. Null when no check-in is scheduled.

nextCheckInLatest.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the latest acceptable next check-in (nextCheckIn plus the check-in margin). Null when no check-in is scheduled.

activeIncident.description: Currently active incident for this environment. Null when the environment is healthy.

startingTimestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the active incident started.

resolvingTimestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the active incident started resolving. Null while the incident is unresolved.

brokenNotice.description: Notification state of the active incident. Null when no broken notice has been issued.

userNotifiedTimestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when users were notified about the broken monitor environment. Null while no notification has been sent.

environmentMutedTimestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the broken monitor environment was muted. Null while it is not muted.

anyOf.description: Notification state for a broken monitor environment.
Currently active incident of a monitor environment.

items.description: Per-environment state of the monitor.

environments.description: Per-environment state of the monitor. Empty until the monitor receives a check-in for an environment.

owner.description: User or team that owns the monitor. Null when the monitor is unassigned.

id.description: ID of the owning user or team.

name.description: Display name of the owning user or team.

type.description: Whether the monitor is owned by a 'user' or a 'team'.

email.description: Email address of the owning user. Only present for user owners.

anyOf.description: User or team that owns the monitor.

Monitor.description: A Sentry cron monitor, including its schedule configuration and nested per-environment state.

actions.description: Permanently delete a set of issues by their IDs.
actions.name: bulk-delete-issues

organization_id_or_slug.description: The ID or slug of the organization that owns the issues. Example: "nangodev".

items.description: Numeric issue ID. Example: "7761433611".

ids.description: The list of issue IDs to permanently delete.

ActionInput_sentry_bulkdeleteissues.description: Input for permanently deleting a set of issues by their IDs.

success.description: True when Sentry accepted the bulk deletion request (HTTP 204). Sentry also returns 204 when some or all IDs matched no issue, so this does not guarantee every listed issue was deleted.

ActionOutput_sentry_bulkdeleteissues.description: Result of the bulk issue deletion request.

actions.description: Update the given field(s) on up to 1000 issues at once, selected by id or by the current search query.
actions.name: bulk-update-issues

organization_id_or_slug.description: The ID or slug of the organization the issues belong to. Example: "my-org".

ids.description: Numeric issue IDs to update, as decimal strings (matching the id field returned by the list-issues actions), sent as repeated id query parameters. Required for non-status updates; optional for status updates, where omitting it updates all issues matching the filters. Maximum 1000. Example: ["123456789"].

query.description: Search query selecting issues when ids is omitted (status updates only). The provider defaults to "is:unresolved" when unset; pass an empty string to match all issues. Example: "is:unresolved browser:Chrome".

project.description: Project IDs or slugs restricting the selection. Omit to include all accessible projects; "-1" also selects all accessible projects. Example: ["web-frontend", "123456789"].

environment.description: Environment names to filter the selection by. Example: ["production"].

statsPeriod.description: Time window for the selection query, a number followed by d, h, m, s, or w. Overrides start and end. Example: "24h".

start.description: ISO-8601 start of the selection time window. Example: "2026-01-01T00:00:00".

end.description: ISO-8601 end of the selection time window. Example: "2026-01-02T00:00:00".

limit.description: Maximum number of issues affected when selecting via filters. Provider maximum is 100.

inbox.description: If true, marks the issues as reviewed by the requestor.

status.description: New status for the selected issues.

inNextRelease.description: If true, marks the issues as resolved in the next release.

inRelease.description: Release version the issues are resolved in. The value "latest" resolves them in the most recent release.

inCommit.description: Commit the issues should be marked as resolved in.

commit.description: SHA of the resolving commit. Example: "2bcba4a1e2932e7b3a0fdd2a68d20c34e8f1a2b3".

repository.description: Name of the repository as it appears in Sentry. Example: "my-org/my-repo".

ignoreDuration.description: Ignore the issues for this many minutes.

ignoreCount.description: Ignore the issues until each has occurred this many times within ignoreWindow minutes.

ignoreWindow.description: Window in minutes over which ignoreCount is measured. Maximum 10080 (1 week).

ignoreUserCount.description: Ignore the issues until each has affected this many users within ignoreUserWindow minutes.

ignoreUserWindow.description: Window in minutes over which ignoreUserCount is measured. Maximum 10080 (1 week).

statusDetails.description: Additional details about the resolution. Status detail updates that include release data are only allowed for issues within a single project.

substatus.description: New substatus for the selected issues; null clears it.

hasSeen.description: If true, marks the issues as seen by the requestor.

isBookmarked.description: If true, bookmarks the issues for the requestor; false removes the bookmark.

isPublic.description: If true, publishes the issues with a public share link; false unpublishes them.

isSubscribed.description: If true, subscribes the requestor to the issues.

merge.description: If true, merges the selected issues together. This cannot be undone.

discard.description: If true, discards the selected issues instead of updating them. Discarded issues are deleted and matching future events are dropped.

assignedTo.description: User or team to assign the issues to, as "<user_id>", "user:<user_id>", "<username>", "<user_primary_email>", or "team:<team_id>". Pass an empty string to unassign.

priority.description: Priority to set on the selected issues.

ignoreDuration.description: Ignore the issues for this many minutes.

actions.description: Get event counts for the organization grouped and time-bucketed by an arbitrary dimension (category, project, outcome, etc.).

field.description: Aggregation to compute per group and interval. "sum(quantity)" is the event count (bytes for attachments); "sum(times_seen)" counts how many times an event has been seen.

statsPeriod.description: Relative time window in <number><unit> format, e.g. "24h" or "7d" (units: m, h, d, w). Provide either this or both start and end; defaults to the last 90 days.

interval.description: Resolution of the time series in the same <number><unit> format as statsPeriod. At most "1d", and must evenly divide one day (1440 minutes), e.g. "1h", "6h", "12h", "1d".

start.description: Start of the time window as a UTC ISO 8601 datetime or epoch seconds. Use together with end instead of statsPeriod. Example: "2026-09-28T00:00:00Z".

end.description: Inclusive end of the time window as a UTC ISO 8601 datetime or epoch seconds. Use together with start instead of statsPeriod.

project.description: Project IDs to filter by. Use ["-1"] to include all accessible projects. Example: ["4512170111991808"].

category.description: Filter by data category, e.g. "error" for error events or "transaction" for transaction events. "attachment", "profile_duration", "profile_duration_ui" and "profile_chunk_ui" cannot be combined with other categories.

outcome.description: Filter by outcome status, e.g. "accepted" for stored events or "rate_limited" for events dropped by rate limiting.

reason.description: Filter by the reason events were filtered or dropped, e.g. "spike_protection".

ActionInput_sentry_getorganizationeventc.description: Dimensions, aggregation field, time window, and filters for the organization event-counts query.

start.description: Start of the resolved time window as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

end.description: End of the resolved time window as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

by.description: Values of the requested groupBy dimensions for this group, e.g. {"category": "error"} or {"project": 4512170111991808, "outcome": "accepted"}.

totals.description: Total for each requested field (keyed by field name, e.g. "sum(quantity)") across the entire time window.

series.description: Per-interval value for each requested field, aligned with the top-level intervals array. Omitted when grouping by project, which returns totals only.

items.description: Event counts for one distinct combination of groupBy dimension values.

groups.description: One entry per distinct combination of groupBy dimension values found in the time window.

groupID.description: Numeric ID of the issue (group) this event belongs to; omitted when the event is not grouped into an issue

title.description: Human-readable event title, e.g. "TypeError: undefined is not a function"

message.description: Event message as sent by the SDK

location.description: File or function location where the event occurred

culprit.description: Function or module Sentry identified as the cause of the event

platform.description: SDK platform that sent the event, e.g. "node"

dateCreated.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when Sentry ingested the event, e.g. "2026-09-29T15:04:05.000Z"; omitted on the rare event Sentry cannot date

eventType.description: Sentry event type, e.g. "error" or "default" (maps the provider field "event.type")

user.description: User context attached to the event, when Sentry could associate one

id.description: ID of the user associated with the event, when known

email.description: Email address of the user associated with the event, when known

username.description: Username of the user associated with the event, when known

ip_address.description: IP address of the user associated with the event, when known

name.description: Display name of the user associated with the event, when known

geo.description: Approximate geolocation (country, region, city) derived from the user IP address

data.description: Additional free-form user attributes sent with the event

tags.description: Tags attached to the event

items.description: Key/value tag attached to the event

crashFile.description: Reference to an attached crash file (e.g. minidump), when present

metadata.description: Free-form event metadata as returned by Sentry (e.g. title, filename, function)

Event.description: A Sentry event ingested by a project (summary payload; the full event body with stacktrace is not included)

syncs.description: Sync issues (error groups) across all projects in the organization.
syncs.name: issues

id.description: Numeric issue ID as a string; used in Sentry API path parameters. Example: "7761433611"

shortId.description: Human-readable issue short ID shown in the Sentry UI and permalinks. Example: "NANGO-SEED-PROJECT-1"

title.description: Issue title, usually the error type and value. Example: "TypeError: undefined is not a function"

culprit.description: Legacy culprit string describing where the error occurred.

permalink.description: URL of the issue details page in Sentry.

level.description: Severity level of the issue. Example: "error"

status.description: Resolution status of the issue: "unresolved", "resolved" or "ignored".

substatus.description: Sub-status of the issue, e.g. "archived_until_escalating" for ignored issues.

logger.description: Logger that reported the issue's events, when set.

platform.description: Platform of the events grouped into this issue. Example: "node"

type.description: Grouping type of the issue, e.g. "error" or "default".

priority.description: Issue priority: "high", "medium" or "low".

count.description: Number of events grouped into this issue, serialized as a string. Example: "150"

userCount.description: Number of distinct users affected by this issue.

numComments.description: Number of comments on the issue.

isPublic.description: Whether the issue has been shared publicly.

isBookmarked.description: Whether the token's user has bookmarked the issue.

isSubscribed.description: Whether the token's user is subscribed to the issue.

hasSeen.description: Whether the token's user has seen the issue.

isUnhandled.description: Whether the issue's events were unhandled exceptions.

annotations.description: Annotation strings attached to the issue, e.g. rendered links to external issues.

project.description: The Sentry project the issue belongs to.

id.description: Numeric ID (as a string) of the project the issue belongs to. Example: "4512170111991808"

slug.description: Slug of the project, unique within the organization. Example: "nango-seed-project"

platform.description: Platform key of the project. Example: "node"

metadata.description: Issue metadata extracted from the ingested event payload.

title.description: Human-readable title generated by Sentry for the issue.

type.description: Error type for error issues, usually the exception class. Example: "TypeError"

value.description: Error value or message for error issues. Example: "undefined is not a function"

filename.description: File in which the error occurred, when known.

function.description: Function in which the error occurred, when known.

assignedTo.description: User or team the issue is currently assigned to. Omitted when unassigned.

type.description: Type of the assignee actor, either "user" or "team". Example: "user"

id.description: ID of the assigned user or team, as a string. Example: "15174593"

name.description: Display name of the assigned user or team. Example: "John Doe"

email.description: Email of the assigned user. Present for user assignees only. Example: "john.doe@example.com"

firstRelease.description: The first release in which the issue was seen, when the issue is bound to a release.

version.description: Version string of the release. Example: "nango-seed-1.0.0"

firstSeen.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the first event grouped into this issue. Example: "2018-11-06T21:19:55Z"

lastSeen.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the most recent event grouped into this issue. Example: "2018-12-06T21:19:55Z"

Issue.description: A Sentry issue (error group) from any project in the organization.

syncs.description: Sync organization members.
syncs.name: members

id.description: Unique ID of the organization membership, e.g. 15174593.

email.description: Email address the membership is bound to, e.g. api@nango.dev.

name.description: Display name of the member. Defaults to the email address.

orgRole.description: Organization-level role of the member, e.g. owner, manager, member or billing.

pending.description: Whether the membership invite is still pending acceptance.

expired.description: Whether the membership invite has expired.

inviteStatus.description: Invite approval status, e.g. approved, requested_to_be_invited or requested_to_join.

inviterName.description: Name of the member who sent the invite, or null when the member was not invited by anyone.

dateCreated.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the membership was created, e.g. 2026-09-29T14:09:02.084485Z.

id.description: Unique ID of the linked Sentry user account, e.g. 5026258.

name.description: Display name of the user. Defaults to the email address.

username.description: Username of the user. Defaults to the email address.

email.description: Email address of the user, e.g. api@nango.dev.

avatarUrl.description: URL of the user avatar image.

isActive.description: Whether the user account is active.

has2fa.description: Whether the user has two-factor authentication enabled.

isManaged.description: Whether the user account is managed by an external identity provider.

isStaff.description: Whether the user is a Sentry staff account.

isSuperuser.description: Whether the user is a Sentry superuser.

isSuspended.description: Whether the user account is suspended.

hasPasswordAuth.description: Whether the user can authenticate with a password.

dateJoined.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the user account was created, e.g. 2026-09-29T14:09:00.725342Z.

lastLogin.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last login, or null if the user has never logged in.

lastActive.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last user activity, or null if the user has never been active.

anyOf.description: Sentry user account linked to the membership.

user.description: Sentry user account linked to the membership, or null while the invite is pending and no user account is linked yet.

Member.description: A Sentry organization member with its organization role and, once the invite is accepted, the linked user account.

syncs.description: Sync cron monitors for a Sentry organization, including schedule configuration and nested monitor environments.
syncs.name: monitors

id.description: Unique Sentry ID of the cron monitor (UUID).

slug.description: URL-safe slug of the monitor, unique within the organization.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the monitor (e.g. 'active', 'disabled', 'pending_deletion').

isMuted.description: Whether the monitor is muted and does not create issues.

isUpserting.description: Whether the monitor was created implicitly by a check-in upsert.

dateCreated.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the monitor was created.

schedule_type.description: Schedule syntax used by the monitor: 'crontab' for a crontab expression or 'interval' for a fixed interval.

schedule.description: Crontab expression (e.g. '0 * * * *') when schedule_type is 'crontab', or a [count, unit] tuple (e.g. [1, 'day']) when schedule_type is 'interval'.

checkin_margin.description: Minutes after the expected check-in time before the check-in is considered missed. Null when the monitor uses the Sentry default.

max_runtime.description: Minutes a check-in may stay in progress before it is considered failed. Null when the monitor uses the Sentry default.

timezone.description: IANA time zone the crontab schedule is evaluated in (e.g. 'America/Los_Angeles'). Null when unset.

failure_issue_threshold.description: Number of consecutive failed check-ins before an issue is created. Null when disabled.

recovery_threshold.description: Number of consecutive successful check-ins before a monitor issue is resolved. Null when disabled.

alert_rule_id.description: Legacy ID of the alert rule attached to this monitor. Null when no alert rule is attached.

config.description: Schedule and check-in tolerance configuration of the monitor.

id.description: Numeric Sentry ID of the project the monitor belongs to.

slug.description: URL-safe slug of the project the monitor belongs to.

name.description: Display name of the project the monitor belongs to.

platform.description: SDK platform key of the project (e.g. 'node'). Null when the project has no platform set.

project.description: Project the monitor belongs to.

status.description: Health status of the monitor in this environment (e.g. 'ok', 'error', 'missed_checkin').

isMuted.description: Whether the monitor environment is muted and does not create issues.

dateCreated.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the monitor environment was created.

lastCheckIn.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent check-in in this environment. Null when no check-in was ever received.

nextCheckIn.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the next check-in is expected in this environment. Null when no check-in is scheduled.

nextCheckInLatest.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the latest acceptable next check-in (nextCheckIn plus the check-in margin). Null when no check-in is scheduled.

activeIncident.description: Currently active incident for this environment. Null when the environment is healthy.

startingTimestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the active incident started.

resolvingTimestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the active incident started resolving. Null while the incident is unresolved.

brokenNotice.description: Notification state of the active incident. Null when no broken notice has been issued.

userNotifiedTimestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when users were notified about the broken monitor environment. Null while no notification has been sent.

environmentMutedTimestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the broken monitor environment was muted. Null while it is not muted.

anyOf.description: Notification state for a broken monitor environment.
Currently active incident of a monitor environment.

items.description: Per-environment state of the monitor.

environments.description: Per-environment state of the monitor. Empty until the monitor receives a check-in for an environment.

owner.description: User or team that owns the monitor. Null when the monitor is unassigned.

id.description: ID of the owning user or team.

name.description: Display name of the owning user or team.

type.description: Whether the monitor is owned by a 'user' or a 'team'.

email.description: Email address of the owning user. Only present for user owners.

anyOf.description: User or team that owns the monitor.

Monitor.description: A Sentry cron monitor, including its schedule configuration and nested per-environment state.

actions.description: Update a client's fields (partial merge), including deactivating it via active:false - the only confirmed way to 'remove' a client since no delete endpoint exists.

actions.description: Send one or more coding-activity heartbeats in a single call (up to 25 per request, per WakaTime's documented limit).
actions.name: create-heartbeats-bulk

entity.description: Entity the heartbeat logs time against, such as an absolute file path, app name, URL, or domain. Example: "/home/user/project/src/index.ts"

type.description: Type of the entity. One of "file", "app", "url", or "domain".

time.description: UNIX epoch timestamp in seconds for when the activity occurred; fractional seconds are allowed. Example: 1700000000.5

category.description: Activity category. Example: "coding". Normally inferred from type when omitted.

project.description: Project name. A project that does not already exist is created automatically. Example: "my-project"

project_root_count.description: Number of folders in the project root path. Example: 5

branch.description: Version control branch name. Example: "main"

dependencies.description: Comma separated list of dependencies detected in the entity file. Example: "react,axios"

lines.description: Total number of lines in the entity when type is "file".

ai_line_changes.description: Number of lines added or removed by GenAI since the last heartbeat in the current file.

human_line_changes.description: Number of lines added or removed by typing since the last heartbeat in the current file.

ai_session.description: AI session id associated with this heartbeat.

ai_input_tokens.description: Number of user input tokens used since the last heartbeat by GenAI tools.

ai_output_tokens.description: Number of output tokens used since the last heartbeat by GenAI tools.

ai_prompt_length.description: Number of user prompt characters typed to AI since the last heartbeat.

ai_subscription_plan.description: Subscription plan for the GenAI tool used for this heartbeat.

lineno.description: Current line row number of the cursor, starting at 1.

cursorpos.description: Current cursor column position, starting at 1.

is_write.description: Whether the heartbeat was triggered by writing to a file.

heartbeats.description: Heartbeats to send in a single request. WakaTime accepts between 1 and 25 heartbeats per call.

ActionInput_wakatime_createheartbeatsbul.description: Input for sending one or more coding-activity heartbeats to WakaTime in a single bulk request.

id.description: Server-generated id of the created heartbeat, present when the heartbeat was accepted. Use it later to delete the heartbeat.

status_code.description: Per-heartbeat HTTP status code WakaTime returned inside the bulk response. Example: 201 for an accepted heartbeat.

skip.description: Reason WakaTime skipped creating this heartbeat, if any. Example: "Too many duplicate heartbeats."

error.description: Provider error message when this heartbeat was rejected, if any.

errors.description: Per-field validation errors when this heartbeat was rejected, keyed by field name. Example: {"type": ["Not a valid choice."]}

results.description: One result per submitted heartbeat, in the same order as the input heartbeats.

ActionOutput_wakatime_createheartbeatsbu.description: Per-heartbeat results of the bulk create request, one entry per submitted heartbeat.

actions.description: Permanently delete one or more heartbeats on a given day by their IDs.
actions.name: delete-heartbeats-bulk

date.description: Day to delete heartbeats from, in YYYY-MM-DD format, interpreted in the user's timezone. Example: "2026-10-10"

ids.description: Heartbeat IDs to delete. Obtain them from the create-heartbeats-bulk response or from list-heartbeats.

ActionInput_wakatime_deleteheartbeatsbul.description: Heartbeats to permanently delete from a single day.

date.description: The day the deletion was scoped to, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

deleted_ids.description: Requested heartbeat IDs that were present for the given day before the deletion and are gone after it.

not_found_ids.description: Requested heartbeat IDs that were not present for the given day before the deletion, usually because the ID or date is wrong; a heartbeat created moments ago may also land here before it becomes visible.

remaining_ids.description: Requested heartbeat IDs still present for the given day after the deletion; empty when every found heartbeat was removed.

ActionOutput_wakatime_deleteheartbeatsbu.description: Result of the bulk heartbeat deletion, including which requested IDs were removed.

actions.description: Permanently delete a project record by its ID.
actions.name: delete-project

project_id.description: The WakaTime project ID to permanently delete. Get it from the "id" field returned by the list-projects action. Example: "9a1b2c3d-4e5f-6789-abcd-ef0123456789".

ActionInput_wakatime_deleteproject.description: Input for deleting a WakaTime project by its ID.

ActionOutput_wakatime_deleteproject.description: Always null. The provider returns no payload for a successful deletion.

total_seconds.description: Total number of seconds logged since the account was created; omitted while still calculating. Example: 0

text.description: Total time logged since the account was created, in human-readable form. Example: "0 secs"

decimal.description: Total coding activity in decimal hours, as a string. Example: "0.00"

digital.description: Total coding activity in digital clock format. Example: "0:00"

daily_average.description: Average coding activity per day in seconds across the range; omitted while still calculating. Example: 0

is_up_to_date.description: Whether the totals are fully calculated; false means they are still being refreshed and may be incomplete

percent_calculated.description: How complete the calculation is, from 0 to 100, where 100 includes today's activity

range.description: The date range the totals cover, from account creation through today

start.description: Start of the range as an ISO 8601 UTC datetime. Example: "2026-10-06T21:00:00Z"

start_date.description: Day the account was created in YYYY-MM-DD format. Example: "2026-10-07"

start_text.description: Day the account was created in human-readable format. Example: "Wed Oct 7th 2026"

end.description: End of the range (end of today) as an ISO 8601 UTC datetime. Example: "2026-10-10T20:59:59Z"

end_date.description: Today in YYYY-MM-DD format. Example: "2026-10-10"

timezone.description: Timezone used for the range in Olson Country/Region format. Example: "Africa/Nairobi"

timeout.description: Keystroke timeout setting in minutes used to join heartbeats into durations

message.description: Explanatory message from WakaTime, present when the stats are still being calculated

ActionOutput_wakatime_getalltimesincetod.description: The user's total coding time since the account was created, plus calculation status.

actions.description: List time-tracking entries across the whole account.

end.description: Range end as an ISO 8601 UTC instant, e.g. "2026-10-08T00:00:00Z".
